brief.title: The History of Books: From Manuscripts to Mass Production
brief.one_liner: A data-driven look at how book production evolved from rare handwritten manuscripts to millions of printed titles over the past 1,500 years.
brief.goal: The viewer should understand the dramatic transformation in book production triggered by the printing press, appreciate the long-term trends in manuscript and book output across centuries, and recognize books as a proxy for literacy, wealth, and cultural development.

sections.title: The Manuscript Era (6th–15th Century)
sections.objective: Show how manuscript production grew slowly over nearly a millennium before the printing press, highlighting the scarcity and luxury status of written works.

sections.title: The Gutenberg Revolution (~1440)
sections.objective: Illustrate the explosive impact of the printing press on book production, with data on printed books per half century from the 15th century onward.

sections.title: Modern Book Publishing & Consumption
sections.objective: Present per-capita metrics on new book titles published and annual book consumption, showing wide variation across countries.

sections.title: Books as a Mirror of Society
sections.objective: Convey the idea that book production data reflects broader trends in literacy, income, education, religion, and cultural development.
